**Visual Analysis:**

- **Plant part affected:** Wheat leaf (narrow, elongated grass leaf held between fingers)
- **Key features:**
  - Small, round, raised pustules scattered across the leaf surface (visible on the underside)
  - Pustules are orange-brown to reddish-brown in color — classic "rust" coloration
  - Pustules are scattered randomly/irregularly (not arranged in stripes or rows)
  - Pustule size is small (~1-2mm), typical of leaf rust uredinia
  - No stripe pattern (rules out Stripe Rust)
  - Pustules are not large/elongated/dark (rules out Stem Rust)
  - No tan lesions with yellow halos (rules out Tan Spot)
  - No powdery white coating (rules out Powdery Mildew)

**Reasoning:**
The image shows classic symptoms of **Wheat Leaf Rust** (*Puccinia triticina*): small, round, orange-brown urediniospore pustules randomly scattered on the wheat leaf surface. The pustule morphology, color, size, and random distribution are hallmarks of leaf rust — distinct from stripe rust (which forms yellow stripe patterns) and stem rust (which has larger, darker, more elongated pustules primarily on stems).
